findings.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.ts:52 — runShardSplitQuery` calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` once per query up front, then `splitQueriesByStreamShard` invokes the nested `runSplitQuery` (shardQuerySplitting.ts:163) once per shard group/cycle, and `runSplitQuery` (querySplitting.ts:299) calls `applyTemplateVariables` again with the same `scopedVars`/`filters` on the already-interpolated, shard-selector-augmented query — the updated test (shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:112, expecting 5 calls for one query across 4 shard cycles) confirms this repeated invocation; if ad-hoc filter injection inside `applyTemplateVariables` is not idempotent (e.g. unconditionally appends a label matcher per filter), each extra pass duplicates the ad-hoc filter's matcher in the stream selector sent to Loki.

public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.ts:52 — runShardSplitQuery` calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` once per query, then hands the (already-interpolated) targets into `runSplitQuery` via `subRequest` (shardQuerySplitting.ts:154,163), which itself calls `applyTemplateVariables` again for every shard sub-request (querySplitting.ts:299), so scopedVars/ad-hoc `filters` interpolation runs twice per query — risking duplicated ad-hoc filter label injection on real (non-idempotent) implementations — and no test in this diff sets a non-empty `request.filters` to check for duplication.

public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:112 — The updated assertion `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` (replacing the old `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` for `interpolateVariablesInQueries`) is a change-detector test: it records that interpolation now runs once per shard-group sub-request plus once up front, but nothing in the test explains or locks in why 5 (i.e., N+1) calls is correct rather than an accidental regression from the double-interpolation path described above.

public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:56 — The `applyTemplateVariables` mock mutates `query.expr` in place (`query.expr = query.expr.replace('$SELECTOR', '{a="b"}'); return query;`) and is idempotent (a second call is a no-op once `$SELECTOR` is gone), so the test suite cannot detect the double-invocation from finding above even though the call count grew from 1 to 5 — a real, non-idempotent implementation that appends ad-hoc filters or mutates shared query objects each call would behave very differently from this mock.

public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.test.ts:75 — The new "Interpolates queries before execution" test (and its shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:84 counterpart) only exercises `$__auto`/`$step` substitution via a hand-rolled idempotent `replace` stub and never sets `request.scopedVars` or a non-empty `request.filters`, so the third `filters` argument added to every `applyTemplateVariables` call site is entirely unverified — no assertion ties ad-hoc filters to the resulting interpolated `expr`.

goldens.comment: The applyTemplateVariables method is called with request.filters as the third parameter, but this parameter is not used in the corresponding test setup.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `runShardSplitQuery` now applies `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` to each target up front (shardQuerySplitting.ts) and `runSplitQuery` also applies `applyTemplateVariables(...)` again to its incoming `request.targets` (querySplitting.ts). The updated test expectation (`applyTemplateVariables` called 5 times) corroborates repeated invocations during shard splitting. However, the claim that this necessarily duplicates ad-hoc filter matchers cannot be verified from the diff because the implementation/idempotency of `applyTemplateVariables` and the internals of `splitQueriesByStreamShard` aren’t shown here; the issue is a concrete, diff-grounded concern about repeated interpolation/side effects, not a proven defect.

adjudication.rationale: In `shardQuerySplitting.test.ts`, the assertion was changed to `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)`, which hard-codes a specific internal call count without documenting why 5 is the correct contract. From the diff, `runShardSplitQuery()` itself only applies `applyTemplateVariables` via a single `.map(...)` over filtered `request.targets` (which is typically 1 target in these tests), so the “5 calls” expectation appears to depend on additional, non-obvious downstream behavior (not shown in this diff) and risks becoming a brittle change-detector rather than asserting externally meaningful behavior (e.g., that the executed query is interpolated).

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:56 — The `applyTemplateVariables` mock mutates `query.expr` in place (`query.expr = query.expr.replace('$SELECTOR', '{a="b"}'); return query;`) and is idempotent (a second call is a no-op once `$SELECTOR` is gone), so the test suite cannot detect the double-invocation from finding above even though the call count grew from 1 to 5 — a real, non-idempotent implementation that appends ad-hoc filters or mutates shared query objects each call would behave very differently from this mock.

adjudication.rationale: In shardQuerySplitting.test.ts the mocked datasource.applyTemplateVariables mutates the LokiQuery object in place (e.g., `query.expr = query.expr.replace(...)` and returns the same `query`). In the production change, runShardSplitQuery now maps over `request.targets` and passes the same query objects into applyTemplateVariables (`.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, ...))`). An in-place, idempotent mock can mask problems that would appear with a real implementation that is non-idempotent or that clones/augments queries, especially when applyTemplateVariables is called multiple times (the test now expects 5 calls). This is a test fidelity concern rather than a directly verifiable runtime defect from the diff.
